heading: The families they married
lead: Seventy-one surnames married into this one, across two hundred and twenty-one recorded marriages. Until now they were a list with counts against it. This page asks a different question of each of them: **which empire held the town this family came from — and therefore which archive has them.**
why: That question matters more than it sounds. On 13 September 2026 this archive learned, the hard way, that **Fiume and Bakar were Hungarian crown land** and that their office-holders sit in Hungarian state paperwork, invisible to every Austrian and Croatian portal the project had been using for a year. The same logic applies to every family below. A name from the Vinodol and a name from Gračišće are forty kilometres apart and **in two different legal worlds**, with two different sets of surviving records. Looking for both in the Croatian parish books alone is why some of these families have stayed blank.

istria-austrian.label: Austrian Istria — the Küstenland
istria-austrian.places: Gračišće · Gologorica · Pazin · Volosca · Vižinada · Svetvinčenat · Vodnjan · Ližnjan
istria-austrian.held: Habsburg from 1797 (Venetian before it), the **Austrian Littoral** from 1849, Italian 1920, Yugoslav 1945, Croatian 1991.
istria-austrian.registers: **Državni arhiv u Pazinu**, and the parish books on FamilySearch film.
istria-austrian.beyond: **ANNO** (Austrian National Library newspapers) and **ALEX** (the imperial *Hof- und Staatshandbuch*) for anyone who held office; the Vienna **Kriegsarchiv** for conscripts. This is the branch the archive knows best.
istria-austrian.gap: ALEX is behind a security check that will not clear for this archive. It has never been read.

hungarian-littoral.label: The Hungarian Littoral
hungarian-littoral.places: Fiume (Rijeka) · Bakar (Buccari) · the Vinodol — Klenovica, Crikvenica, Ledenice, Novi · Senj
hungarian-littoral.held: **Hungarian crown land**, not Austrian — a separate legal world with its own ministries, budgets and civil service.
hungarian-littoral.registers: **Državni arhiv u Rijeci** and the parish books.
hungarian-littoral.beyond: **Hungaricana** — free, full-text, and the single most under-used source this archive has. State final accounts naming pensioners and their orphans; parliamentary pension schedules with years of service; the National Archives of Hungary plan collection. **This is where the office-holders are**, and they are in none of the Austrian or Croatian portals.
hungarian-littoral.gap: Barely begun. Opened for the first time on 13 September 2026.

dalmatia.label: Austrian Dalmatia
dalmatia.places: Zadar · Šibenik · Split · Omiš · Postira · Dubrovnik · Seget
dalmatia.held: Venetian to 1797, then Habsburg as the **Kingdom of Dalmatia**, governed from Zadar by a Luogotenenza answering to Vienna.
dalmatia.beyond: The **Namjesništvo / Luogotenenza** fond at Zadar — the governor's office, which watched the press and the politically suspect and wrote down what it saw. One file in it has just given this archive Valente Defranceschi. **Political-police fonds are indexed by name and almost wholly unworked for this surname.**
dalmatia.gap: One errand queued; nothing yet requested.

carnia.label: Carnia and Friuli
carnia.places: Ovaro · Mione · Muina · Paluzza · Tolmezzo · Sequals · Lestans · Pinzano
carnia.registers: **Archivio di Stato di Udine**, and the parish archives; the pre-1806 Ovaro books are in no portal at all.
carnia.beyond: **Antenati** (the Italian state archives portal) for the civil registration from 1806 — but it 403s this archive and its name search is behind a bot check. The Austrian decades 1815–66 should leave Habsburg administrative traces that nobody has looked for.
carnia.gap: The largest hole in the archive. **Fourteen of the seventy-one in-married families carry Carnian surnames** — which is either the strongest circumstantial support the Carnia origin has, or a surname-morphology illusion. It has never been tested against a Carnian register.

venice.label: Venice and the Veneto
venice.places: Venice · Castelgomberto and Cornedo in Vicenza · Ponte nelle Alpi in Belluno · Pederobba in Treviso
venice.held: The Republic to 1797; Austrian; Italian from 1866.
venice.registers: **Archivio di Stato di Venezia** and the provincial state archives.
venice.beyond: Antenati again, with the same block. The Venetian state archive's own series are catalogued online but not imaged.
venice.gap: Never systematically searched for the in-married names.

rows.name: Orlis / Ortis
rows.origin: Novaki, house 2 — the parish north of Gologorica

peschle.from: Volosca, on the Kvarner — and Fiume; with a house at Gologorica and a doctor living at Pazin
peschle.why: **Lambertina Peschle married Josephus de Franceschi at Gologorica on 3 February 1807 and became the mother of Carlo De Franceschi**, the historian this whole archive leans on. She was born about 1786 and died on 16 July 1863; the 1826 status animarum of house 7 records her as *Lambertina*.
known: **Mathias Peschle**, b. 1756, married Justina Jacich.
**Alexander Peschle**, b. 1803, son of Mathias and Justina, married Franca Descovich.
**Alexander Peschle**, b. 1797, married Anna Promagnoli.
**Pasqualina** and **Ercolano Peschle**, their children, at **Fiume**.
**Paschalis Maria Peschle**, b. 28 April 1832, of Alessandro and Anna.
**Carmina Peschle**, 1832–1833, died in infancy.

**Dr Albertus Peschle**, *civis*, head of **Gologorica house 2** in the 1826 status animarum — with his wife **Victoria, née Calligarich**, and their son **Conradus Josephus Victorius, born 20 July 1853**. The adnotatio against him reads ***«habitat Pisini»*** — he kept the house at Gologorica and lived at **Pazin**. *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069322.)*

**Amalia Peschle, *ex VOLOSCA*** — godmother at the baptism of Clementina Maria Defranceschi, **6 October 1822**, standing with Pietro Antonio Defranceschi; both entered *Cives Gollogoricenses*. ⚠ **This archive published her as** «*ex Silesia*» **and built [worklist 170](/worklist/) on it; [re-read at four times magnification on 11 October 2026 the word is](/corrections/)** «***ex Volosca***» — *the Kvarner town where this page already placed the family.* *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069089.)*

**Anselmus Peschle**, godfather *per procuratorem* — by proxy — at the baptism of **Anna Maria Francisca Defranceschi**, 4 November 1860, Gologorica house 7, with **Beatrice Ortis**; both entered *cives*. *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069135, folio 121.)* **He was not in the village that day**, which is what a proxy means.

**Remigius Cæsar Peschle**, born **1 October 1864** at Gologorica house 4, baptised the 9th — son of **Dr Albertus Peschle**, *Doctor medicinæ*, and **Victoria née Calligarich**; godparents **«Luigi De Franceschi»** and **«Celestina V.da Calligarich»**. *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069140, folio 126.)*

**Dr Albertus Peschle stands godfather to a Defranceschi child**, 5 December 1869 — [Robertus Franciscus Josephus](/person/robertus-franciscus-josephus-defranceschi-1860/), son of Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi and Clotildis Ortis at house 7 — with **Maria Defranceschi**, the pair entered *cives*. *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069148, folio 137.)*
peschle.found:
**Fifty-one hits on Hungaricana, and almost all of them are one man.** *Dr **Cäsar Peschle***, a medical officer of the **K. K. Landwehr**, commissioned 1 August 1895 with rank from 5 September 1895, serving as *Assistenzarzt* and then with the 5th and 23rd Regiments, attached to the **Landsturm district of Görz — Gorizia** — and still on the lists in 1918. Twenty-three years of an Austrian army doctor's career, free, page by page.

**⭐ SOMETHING NOW JOINS HIM TO THIS VILLAGE — 5 October 2026.** *The Gologorica baptism register enters* **«REMIGIUS CÆSAR natus 1 Oct.»**, *9 October 1864, house 4, son of* **«Albertus Peschle, Doctor medicinæ»** *and* **«Victoria nata Calligarich»**. *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069140, folio 126.)*

***Four things agree with the man on the army lists at once***: *the surname; the given name, uncommon enough to be worth something; the profession already in the household; and the age —* **a man born in October 1864 is just under thirty-one when that commission is granted in August 1895**, *which is exactly when an* Assistenzarzt *is commissioned after his training.*

**⚠ It is an inference and it is written as one.** *The Hungaricana entries are army lists: rank, regiment and date, no birthplace.* ***Neither record names the other.*** *What this archive has is a Gologorica birth that fits an Austrian career at four points, where before it had a career attached to nothing.* **(inf.)**

**And it changes what the Gorizia coincidence is worth.** *Cäsar Peschle's Landsturm district was* **Gorizia**, *where Carlo De Franceschi was sent to the seminary — recorded here as a coincidence of place and not evidence.* ***It is still not evidence.*** *But a coincidence between two strangers is worth less than a coincidence between a man and his mother's family's village, and this entry is what moves it from the first kind to the second.*

**⚠ AND THE FAMILY WAS THOUGHT TO REACH SILESIA. IT DOES NOT.** *The 1822 entry was read as* **«Amalia Peschle ex Silesia»** *and [the word is* «**ex Volosca**»*](/corrections/). Volosca, Fiume, Gologorica, Pazin — and Volosca again. The paragraph that stood here claimed a direction this archive had no reason to look in.*

**⚠ And the name is written four ways**: *Peschle, **Pesle** (twice in the baptism register), and Peste at page scale, which was a misreading. **No form is preferred.***

**⚠ A HARDER QUESTION WAS RAISED HERE, AND IT IS WITHDRAWN.** *The paragraph that stood here asked whether the Peschle were German-Silesian in origin, so that* «Volosca and Fiume are where they arrived, not where they came from», *and whether Carlo De Franceschi's mother was therefore half German.* ***It rested on a single word, and [the word reads* «**ex Volosca**»*](/corrections/).*** **Nothing else ever supported it**: «Peschle» *not looking Kvarner is an impression, and* **Peschel**, **Peschke** *and* **Pöschl** *being German names is a fact about Germany, not about this family.* ✔ ***The register puts the Peschle at Volosca, which is where this page had them.***

**⭐ 5 OCTOBER 2026 — TWO MORE SIGHTINGS, AND THEY BOTH POINT THE SAME WAY.**

**The doctor's own child, 28 July 1853.** *Dr* **Albertus Peschle**, *D.r Medicinæ, of Gologorica house 2, and* **Victoria née Calligarich** *had a son* **Conradus Josephus Victorius** *— a household this archive already held from the census. What it did not have is who stood for him:* **«Cost. SCHROTT»** *and* **«Carolina WALSER»**, *entered* **cives**. ***Two unmistakably German surnames at an Istrian font, chosen by a Peschle for his own son.*** *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069128, folio 114.)*

**And a fourth Peschle, summoned in absentia.** *At the baptism of* **Anna Maria Francisca Defranceschi**, *4 November 1860, the godfather is* **«ANSELMUS PESCHLE … per procuratorem»** — *by proxy, the formula for a godparent who cannot come and has a stand-in hold the child.* ***Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi wanted a Peschle at his daughter's font badly enough to have one in absentia.*** *(doc — M01069135, folio 121.)*

**So the Peschle of this archive now number four across fifty years at one small village:** *[Lambertina](/who/lambertina-defranceschi-peschle/) who married in; **Amalia «ex Volosca»**; **Dr Albertus**, physician, who kept the house at Gologorica and lived at Pazin; and **Anselmus**, who had to be represented.* ***A dispersed, literate household with reach*** — *which is a description, not an origin.*

**⚠ AND THE CAUTION THAT GOES WITH IT.** *Schrott and Walser are German or Austrian;* **neither is Silesian in particular**, *and neither is tied here to a place. A doctor of medicine in Habsburg Istria moved among German speakers as a matter of course, and a proxy godfather tells you he was away without telling you where.* ⚠ ***There is no Silesia question to answer.*** *[It was withdrawn on 11 October 2026 when the word it rested on was magnified](/corrections/). Schrott and Walser remain two German surnames in a Peschle household's company, and that is all they ever were.*

**⭐ AND THE TWO HOUSES ARE STILL JOINED IN 1869.** *On 5 December 1869* **Dr Albertus Peschle** *himself stands godfather to* **[Robertus Defranceschi](/person/robertus-franciscus-josephus-defranceschi-1860/)** *at house 7, with* «Maria Defranceschi», *both* **cives**. ***A Peschle married into this house in 1807; sixty-two years later a Peschle physician is still at its font.*** *That is not a lead about origins — it is the shape of a relationship, and it is the reason the Peschle keep appearing in a Defranceschi archive at all.*
peschle.next:
Volosca's registers are at Pazin or Rijeka; the Peschle at **Fiume** belong in Hungarian paperwork. **The name is Germanic and the forename is Germanic** — *Lambertina*, for St Lambert of Maastricht, is a Rhineland and Low Countries name, not an Istrian or a Venetian one. A German-named family on the Kvarner in the eighteenth century is most likely an **immigrant administrative or mercantile household**, which is exactly the kind that leaves imperial rather than parish traces.

**⭐ And there is a route to the Peschle that never depended on Silesia.** *The Gologorica register carries a certificate — [«Quae copiae collationatae anni 1835 concordant cum hoc originali libro»](/gologorica-line/) — showing that* ***the parish made a certified copy of each year's register and the dean collated it***. *If the duplicates survive, the Peschle entries exist twice; and [worklist 178](/worklist/) is now the item that would find them.* ⚠ ***The instruction that stood here — to carry* **Schrott**, **Walser** *and* **Anselmus** *into «any Acta Publica sweep» of the Silesian parishes — is withdrawn with [the reading that prompted it](/corrections/).*** *The place to look for the Peschle is* **Volosca and Fiume**, *where the register puts them.*

salomon.why: **Francisca Salomon, born 17 March 1797, married Giovanni Battista Defranceschi** and is the mother of the third generation of our line. Her family had a palace on the square at Gračišće, facing the bishop's.
known: Children recorded: **Raymundus** b. 9 October 1823, **Antonius** b. 20 September 1825 — who carried the line — and **Joannes** b. 30 June 1833.
salomon.found: **Nothing yet in the Hungarian material**, which is the expected answer: Gračišće is Austrian Istria, not Hungarian crown land, so its people belong in Vienna's paperwork and Pazin's, not Budapest's.
salomon.next: A family with a palace on the town square is a family with **property deeds, tax assessments and probably a coat of arms**. The Austrian **Franciscan cadastre** of 1818–20 names the owner of every parcel, and the *Blasonario Giuliano* — already used by this archive for our own name — should be checked for Salomon. Neither has been done.

fernasar.why: **Maria née Fernasar, born 17 October 1832, married Antonio Defranceschi** and is the mother of Josip, who took the line out of Istria to Crikvenica.
known: The surname is written **Fernasar** in one hand and **Tornasar** in another. **Tornasar is now retired** — it appears in not one issue of the Austrian press, in no Italian surname database and in no Croatian census return, while Fernasar is printed three times and placed at Gračišće. The reading stands as **Fernasar**; see below and [the search log](/searched/). *(The two hands are both real: a register entry of 1862 was read «Maria Tornasar», and that reading is kept as a reading.)*
A related puzzle sits beside her: a marriage recorded 25 November 1856 with an eldest son born 6 August 1856, three and a half months earlier.
fernasar.found:
**Found, and placed — in a First World War casualty list, which is a kind of record this archive had never once opened.**

Three spellings were tested against the Austrian press. **«Tornasar» returns nothing at all** — not one issue, not one living bearer — and the second reading this archive carried for a year can be retired. **«Fernasar» returns three issues**, and two of them are Austro-Hungarian casualty lists, which print a man's name, rank, regiment, **home commune** and year of birth.

**«Verlustliste», 6 May 1916:**

> *Fernasar Josef, Inft., k. k. LIR. Nr. 5, 10. Komp., **Istrien, Pisino, Gračišće**, 1884; kriegsgef., **Merw, Gebiet Transkaspien, Rußland**.*

**Josef Fernasar, born 1884, of GRAČIŠĆE** — infantryman of the 5th Imperial-Royal Landwehr Infantry Regiment, 10th Company, **taken prisoner and held at Merv in Transcaspia**, which is now Mary in Turkmenistan. The list gives province, district and **commune**: Istria, Pisino, Gračišće. **That is Maria's own village**, named in a printed record, fifty-two years after she married out of it.

**«Nachrichten über Verwundete und Verletzte», 14 December 1914:**

> *Fernasar Josef, Jäg., FJB. Nr. 20, 1. StbsAbt., **Pisino [I]strien**, 1883, Hufschlag a. d. r. Ferse, Vereinshilfsspital Nr. 2 in Kassa.*

A Josef Fernasar of the Pisino district, born 1883, kicked by a horse on the right heel and in the auxiliary hospital at Kassa. **Whether this is the same man is not settled**: the name, district and rough age agree, the unit and the year do not. One record says Jäger of Field Battalion 20 and 1883; the other says infantryman of Landwehr Regiment 5 and 1884. Men changed units and clerks mis-copied years. **Two cousins would look exactly the same.**

The third issue, *Il Giornaletto di Pola* of 8 December 1914, has not been read.

**And «Fornasar» — 49 issues, overwhelmingly the same Pola paper — remains the commoner form of what is very probably the same Friulian name**: *fornasâr*, the man who works the kiln. That step is still an inference.
fernasar.next:
**The surname is now placed at Gračišće and the question changes.** It is no longer *where were the Fernasar* but *how do they connect to Maria*, born there on 17 October 1832.

Josef of 1884 is two generations below her. The Gračišće status animarum — the household books this archive has already read frame by frame for its own family — **will have the Fernasar households on the same pages**, and nobody has looked for them.

Then *Il Giornaletto di Pola*, 8 December 1914, which is the one Fernasar issue still unread; and the **Gračišće register image** for Maria's own entry, which would settle the letter the priest actually formed.

kalanj.why: **Anna Kalanj, born 3 January 1864, married Josip Defranceschi** — the generation that left Istria. She came from the valley directly above Crikvenica and did not move far.
known: Four marriages of the name into this family in the index.
Two households: **Josip × Ana Kalanj** at **Ledenice** 1890–92, and at **Crikvenica** 1894–96 — the same couple, recorded in two parishes.
kalanj.found: Not yet searched in the Hungarian material — **and it should be.** The Vinodol was in **Modruš-Fiume county, Hungarian crown land**, which is precisely the jurisdiction whose records this archive only opened on 13 September 2026.
kalanj.next: Hungaricana for the surname; the Vinodol parish books at Rijeka. Ledenice and Crikvenica are eight kilometres apart and the family used both.

kovacina.why: **Uršula Kovačina, born at Crikvenica on 28 February 1895, married Anton Rudolf Defranceski** — our fifth generation, the one taken to Pfullingen.
known: **Her own baptism has been read (27 October 2026): born illegitimate to Marija Car, no father named, nine months before her mother married the joiner Petar Kovačina.** She was the nearest wall in the direct line; her mother is now named and her father is the open question.
kovacina.found: Her baptism at Crikvenica, and a margin note giving her death at Belgrade on 3 November 1975. She has still not been searched for outside the Croatian books.
kovacina.next: She married a man of Klenovica, in the Hungarian Littoral, about 1912–24. If she was local, she is in Hungarian-administered parishes and possibly in Hungarian civil paperwork. **Of all the names on this page, hers is the one where a new jurisdiction is most likely to break a wall in our own line.**

bergamo.from: southern Istria — the parish behind «Croazia, Austria»
bergamo.why: **The largest in-marrying family in the whole archive: seventeen marriages.** And it goes both ways — Antonio De Franceschi married **Maria Bergamo** (six children, 1825–45), and **Francesca Defranceschi** married **Giovanni Bergamo** (seven children, 1831–46). Two households, one generation, two directions.
known: This is also where this archive made one of its worst errors: Francisca was published as the wife of Antonius Cerneca, off a tabular register whose four parent columns the index flattens into one list. She married Bergamo. The correction stands.
bergamo.found: Not searched in any imperial source.
bergamo.next: Seventeen marriages into one family across one parish is not chance — it is **two houses intermarrying for a century**, which normally means neighbours or business partners. The Svetvinčenat status animarum would put both households on a street.

bellinich.why: **Catharina Bellinich** married Franciscus Defranceschi at Bakar (three baptisms, 1836), and **Carolina Bellinich** married *Francisci Defranceschi **Regii*** there in 1849 — the twins, and the week that took two children.
known: Almost certainly **one man and two sisters**, the widower marrying his wife's sister; or one woman whose name two indexers read differently.
bellinich.found: Not yet searched — but Bakar is **Hungarian crown land**, and the Hungarian material has already produced the Bakar salt office plan of 1827 and the Royal Hungarian port captain.
bellinich.next: Hungaricana for Bellinich, and the Bakar baptisms, which would settle the one-man-or-two question in a line.

cosulich.from: Lussinpiccolo and Trieste — and then, for fifty years, Cardiff
cosulich.why: **Marietta Cosulich married Emerico De Franceschi at St Peter's, Roath — the Catholic parish of Cardiff — on 26 July 1876**, her father *Josephi Francisci Cosulich* in the priest's genitive. **Cosulich is a Lussinpiccolo and Trieste shipowning house**, and the masters printed beside De Franceschi in the shipping columns of those years — Bujanovich, Lacovich, Cattarinich — are Lussino names to a man.
known: **Giuseppe Cosulich, b. 1829**, and **Giulia, b. 1831**, keeping house at **St John, Cardiff** in the **1881 census** — almost certainly the *Josephi Francisci* of the marriage entry.
**Richiard b. 1860**, **Teny b. 1863**, **Enrico b. 1866** — in that same 1881 household, and so most likely Marietta's brothers and sister.
**Emilio b. 1854** and **Jesse b. 1864**, at St John, Cardiff, in the **1891 census**.
**T. S. Cosulich, b. 1844**, at **St Thomas, Swansea**, in the **1871 census** — the earliest of them in South Wales.
**Giulio A. b. 1860 and Bridget b. 1877**, with **Irene, Felix, Doris, Mabel and Bernard**, at **Barry** in the **1921 census**.
**Bernard S. Cosulich, b. 1916**, in the **1939 Register** at Rhyl.
cosulich.found:
**They are why «an old Cardiff family» is true.** [Searched on 21 September 2026](/searched/): no person of the Defranceschi surname, in any spelling, is enumerated anywhere in Glamorgan in any census from 1841 to 1921 — and the Cosulich are there in 1871, 1881, 1891, 1921 and 1939. **The Cardiff roots in that 1896 newspaper sentence are the bride's, not the groom's.**

**Marietta herself is in none of them.** She married in July 1876 and had left before the 1881 census — the *Aquilone* cleared the Bute Docks for Guadeloupe seventeen months after the wedding, and a master's wife goes where the ship goes.

bembo.from: Valle (Bale), on the west coast of Istria — a Venetian patrician name
bembo.why: **Anna, daughter of the *Nobil Signor* Tommaso Bembo of Valle, married Petrus Defranceschi of Gologorica on 22 January 1795**, the three publications of banns dispensed with by the bishop of Parenzo. *It is the only marriage this archive holds that takes the name into a Venetian patrician house.*
known: **Anna Bembo**, **born 5 July 1779**, wife of Petrus Defranceschi (b. 17 April 1768, d. 1829). *Her birth year was on David's tree; the **day and month come from the Gologorica* status animarum *of 1826**, which also confirms the marriage.* *(doc.)*
**Tommaso Bembo**, her father, styled *«N. Sig.r»* — *Nobil Signor* — in the Valle marriage entry of 1795. **Nothing else is known of him here.**
**Hermenegildus Defranceschi**, their son, **born 4 October 1803** — *new to this archive on 30 September 2026.*
bembo.found: **The household was split across the border.** *A brace in the 1826 census against Anna's row and her son's reads* ***«In partibus Venetias … habitant»*** — **they live in the Venetian parts**, while Petrus is entered at Gologorica. *That is the first thing this archive has learned about the marriage after the wedding day itself.*

jablich.why:
**«Cath. ejus uxor nata Jablich ex Buccari»** — *Catharina, his wife, born Jablich, out of Buccari.* **She is the wife of Joannes Baptista Defranceschi**, and the two of them stand godparents together at Gologorica on **3 October 1786**, both entered as ***Cives Gollogoricenses***.

**This archive had no Catharina as the wife of any Joannes Baptista** — only two daughters of that name — **and the surname Jablich appears nowhere in it at all.**
known: **Catharina Defranceschi, née Jablich, of Buccari (Bakar)**, wife of **Joannes Baptista Defranceschi**, *civis* of Gologorica. Standing godmother with her husband at a Gologorica baptism, **3 October 1786**. *(doc.)*
jablich.found:
**Bakar is not a new place to this archive — it is an old unanswered question.** *The search register has carried **«Bakar's parish registers»** as a standing request for weeks, unopened. **This is the first person who gives a reason to open them**: a woman of Buccari marrying a Defranceschi of Gologorica before 1786, which is a hundred and thirty kilometres and a different sovereignty away from the Istrian interior.*

*⚠ The surname was first read as **Jaklich** at page scale. At five times magnification the letter is a **b**, matching the b of «Buccari» written directly beneath it in the same hand. **Jablich.***

---

**✔✔ 9 October 2026 — the family's own parish spells it SABLICH, and the proof is internal.**

*[The Bakar marriage of 10 November 1783](/gologorica-line/#bakar1783) names the bride's father* «**D. Sabastiani Sablich**» *and the bride* «**D. Catharinam Sablich**». **The same scribe writes** «**Jacobus**» **and** «**Josepho**» **three lines below, both with a long descender below the baseline; the Sablich initial has none** — ***and «Sabastiani» and «Sablich» open with the identical letterform, which in Sebastian can only be an S.*** *(doc — FamilySearch,* «Croatia, Delnice Deanery Catholic Church Books, 1571–1926»: **Bakar, Religious Marriage Registers 1739–1808, film 005494714, image 172, page 161**; *custodian* **Hrvatski državni arhiv u Zagrebu**. *Image downloaded 9 October 2026 at 5975×4206 and read locally.)*

⚠ **Gologorica's own register still writes** «nata **JABLICH** ex Buccari», *and probably wrote exactly that —* ***two scribes, not two readings***. *The heading here keeps both forms because the archive met her under the Istrian one.*

orlis.from: Novaki (Novacis), house 2 — and the family styled *Dominus* by 1813
orlis.why: **Three generations of Ortis stand beside this family, across seventy-two years.** *Matthaeus at the font in* **1787**, *his son* **Dominus Joannes** *in* **1813**, *and* **Clotilda** *marrying Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi — Carlo's brother — in* **1859**. **The connection to Novaki is not the marriage; the marriage is the end of it.**
known: **Matthaeus Ortis of Novaki** — godfather at the Gologorica baptism of **Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, 13 August 1787**, entered *«Matth: Ortis ex Novacco»*. *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069018.)*
**Dominus Joannes Ortis**, *«Dni Matthiae filius, ex Novacco»* — **his son** — godfather in **1813**, both men styled **Dominus**. *(doc — M01069074.)*

**Clotilda**, born **12 October 1834**, died **27 February 1881**. Entered *«Clotilda uxor Ortis, filia Joannis ac Franciscæ»*, and coming *«Ex Parochia Novacis sub N.º 2»*. *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069333.)*
**Joannes** and **Francisca**, her parents, named in that one line and nowhere else here.
**Victor Josephus**, her son with Franciscus Xaverius, born **22 April 1862**.
orlis.found:
**⚠ The name is spelled two ways in two books of the same parish.** *The 1894 *status animarum* gives* **Orlis**; *the 1826 book gives* **Ortis**. **Neither is preferred**, *because this archive's rule is that a hand is only legible against itself and the same scribe has not been found writing both forms. The row carries both until one is settled.*

**Novaki is also where a priest of Gologorica came from** — *Josephus Flegar, born 16 April 1845, in [the succession on the line page](/gologorica-line/). Nothing joins them; it is recorded because the parish is small and the next person should know the name is in both places.*

grach.why:
**This family married into the direct line once, in 1774 — and the archive has since found it living in three parishes within ten kilometres, under three spellings, without yet being able to join any two of them.** *[Theresia née Grach is the mother of the casa 31 household at Gologorica](/person/theresia-defranceschi-nee-grach-gologorica/), and her family produced an archpriest who married her, buried her husband's sister and stood godfather to her son.* ***What follows is everything this archive holds, by parish, with what is not established kept separate at the end.***

**⭐⭐⭐ 11 October 2026 — TWO Grah wives out of the 1862 Gologorica census, and one of them names her house at Cerovlje.** *[One opening (M01069464) carries two Bubić households, each with a Grah wife](/gologorica-line/#twograhwives) — the exact class of person the book's own family index cannot see.*

| | |
|---|---|
| «**Rosalia ux. n. GRAH-MISSAN**» | *n.* **13 Maji 1845**, *m.* **18 Junii 1869** *to* «Franciscus Bubić», *rusticus* · *Adnotatio* «***e Cerovglie N.º 12***» |
| «**Marianna ux. n. GRAH-JOPAN**» | *n.* **19 Sept. 1834**, *m.* **22 Jann. 1861** *to* «Joannes Bubić», *ob.* **19 Agost. 1870** |

✔ ***Rosalia is the* «Grah - Missan Rosalia, house 29, 1845» *of [the 1894 Repertorium](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses)***, *now with a day, a husband, a son and an origin.* ✔✔ **The second of those is now read in a clear hand:** «**GRAH-ŽIPAN**» — *[the Croatian* **župan**, *a village headman, confirmed on a baptism page of 1864 beside* «Grah-Missan» *in the same clerk's writing](/gologorica-line/#grahzipan), and joining [the* «**Suppanus Joannes Grach**» *this archive already holds at Gračišće](/direct-line/).* ⚠ *It was first published as* «Grah-Jopan», *withdrawn, and then settled.* ⚠⚠ **And it belongs to a THIRD woman, not to Marianna** — «**Rosa Grah-Žipan**», *godmother with Josephus Udovičić in 1864; [Marianna is* «**Grah-Missan**» *twice over in the baptism register](/corrections/).* **The older note below is left as it stood** — *the initial does not match this scribe's own* **J** *at magnification, and the word runs into the column rule.* *What is secure is* «Grah-» *and a tall-ascender second element;* **[it may be* župan*, an office, and not a family at all](/gologorica-line/#grahsecond)**.

**⚠ House 12 is not in the Cerovlje book.** *[That sweep found the Grah at houses 18, 19, 23, 38 and 53](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah), and marries its daughters into Držetić, Dujanić, Šepuka, Opašić, Krošnjak and Lušetić —* ***not Bubić***. *Rosalia left in 1869, before those households were drawn.* ***The Gologorica census preserves a Cerovlje Grah house that Cerovlje's own surviving book does not.***
known: **KRBUNE — the family this line actually married.** *Both of the Krbune Grah the archive holds are placed there by the registers' own words,* «ex Parochia **Cherbune**».

**⭐ THERESIA DEFRANCESCHI née GRACH** — *married* **9 June 1774** *at Gologorica, as* «Virgine», *a maiden, so it was her first marriage. [Her roster row carried no note, no date and no source at all until that entry was read](/person/theresia-defranceschi-nee-grach-gologorica/).* ***Four children are now documented***: *[**Josepha Mariana**, born and baptised at Krbune 15 March 1776](/person/mariana-defranceschi-d1786/) — she went home to her own parish to bear her first; [**Joannes Petrus**, 1780](/person/joannes-petrus-defranceschi-1780/); [**Franciscus Antonius**, 13 April 1785](/person/franciscus-antonius-defranceschi-1785/); and [**Joannes Baptista**, 12 August 1787](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-1787/).* *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068999, M01068934, M01069015, M01068946.)*

**⭐ And she is a godmother six times over, 1776–1784**, *twice beside her own husband, who is named* «q.ᵐ Leonardi» *in the same clause — so [the marriage register is no longer the only document joining those two names](/gologorica-line/#mercator1779). On* **16 January 1784** *a baptism register writes her as* «***Theresia Defranceschi nata GRACH***», *ten years after the wedding.*

**⭐ ANTONIUS GRAH of Krbune — Theresia's father**, *named at her marriage:* «*copulatus est cum Virgine* **Theresia, filia Antonij Grah ex Parochia Cherbune**». *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01068999.)* ***A generation above anything this archive held for the Grah.***

**⭐⭐ JOANNES GRAH, Archpriest and Parish Priest of Krbune** — *and this archive can now count* ***six acts*** *for him, all at Gologorica, all for this family or its neighbours:*

| | |
|---|---|
| **9 Jun 1774** | *marries* **Theresia** *to* [Joannes Baptista](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-detti-leonardi-m-1774/) |
| **15 Mar 1776** | *gives leave for* [Josepha Mariana's baptism at Krbune](/person/mariana-defranceschi-d1786/) |
| **9 Aug 1778** | *baptises at Gologorica himself* |
| **25 Apr 1783** | *buries* [**Margaretta Defranceschi**](/person/margarita-defranceschi-1747/) «in Arca Parentuum» |
| **27 May 1784** | *buries* **Leonardus Deprato** — ⚠ *[not this family, and the claim that his acts were all for it was withdrawn](/corrections/)* |
| **13 Apr 1785** | *stands godfather to* [**Franciscus Antonius**](/person/franciscus-antonius-defranceschi-1785/) |

***This page said of him, until 9 October 2026, «he is named by office and surname only; no forename is given», and proposed writing to a diocesan archive for one.*** **The forename was on the family's own hard drive, in the act of marrying the couple.** *[The story.](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774)*
*The 1776 entry also names* «**Joannes Jadreicich, Capellanus Cherbunensis**» — *the chaplain of Krbune, new to this archive.*

⚠⚠ **AND KRBUNE'S OWN REGISTER HAS NO GRAH IN IT AT ALL.** *[1803–1870, a controlled nil with the instrument proved against 457 Valcovich from the same film](/searched/).* ***The book opens thirty years after Antonius and the archpriest are last heard of***, *so the nil says the name had gone from Krbune by 1803 — not that it was never there.*

**GRAČIŠĆE — a household of standing, found 11 October 2026.** *[The baptism register's ruled table was swept frame by frame, M01070190–M01070226, 1784 to May 1808, down every column](/gologorica-line/#grahgracisce).*

**⭐⭐ JOSEPHUS GRAH and DOMINICA, house 174.** *Five children baptised —* **Lucia** *(13 May 1785),* **Francisca** *(25 Jan 1790),* **Franciscus** *(25 May 1792),* **Joannes** *(30 Mar 1794),* **Josephus** *(8 May 1802)* — *and* ***five further appearances as godparents*** *between 1792 and 1796.* ***The conditio column grades them* «Cives» *at all ten.*** *Their children's godparents include two* **Picot** *judges, and* «**Joannes Jerbulla, SUPANUS**» *with* «**Notburga Jerbulla, JUDICISSA**» — *the village headman and the judge's wife.*

**⭐⭐⭐ And a Defranceschi carried one of those children to the font.** *8 May 1802, house 174:* «*Pater* ***Josephus Grah*** · *Mater* ***Dominica Grah*** · *Patrini* ***Joannes Salamon*** *et* ***Theresia Defranceschi*** · ***Cives***» *(ZM34K-215, M01070218).* ***Three of this archive's surnames in one clause.*** ⚠ *[This archive had already cited that frame](/gologorica-line/) — for the Defranceschi godmother — because it read the Patrini column for one surname and never looked at the Pater column beside it.*
*Also* «**Anna Zulle olim GRAH**» *(31 January 1787, house 46) — a Grah daughter married into the Zulle.*
**CEROVLJE — NINE households, and the largest population of the name anywhere.** *[Its* status animarum *is now read end to end, all 138 frames](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah).*

**⭐⭐⭐ HOUSE 18 — four generations in one door.**

| | |
|---|---|
| «**GRAH Mathias def. Mathiae**», *rusticus* | *n.* **15 Aug 1837** · *m.* **26 Jan 1863** · *ob.* **10 Sept 1929**, *with* «**Maria n. KROŠNJAK**», *n.* **1 Jul 1839**, *ob.* **5 Nov 1908** |
| «**Grah Matthaeus fil. Mathiae**», *rusticus* | *n.* **21 Nov 1863** · *ob.* **26 Oct 1940**, *with* «**Maria n. GRŽEVIĆ**», *n.* **31 Oct 1868**, *ob.* **14 Nov 1938** — ***nine children, 1892–1909*** |
| «**Grah Antonius**», *agricola* | *n.* **7 May 1900** · *ob.* **11 Dec 1970**, *with* «**Rosaria n. FLEGAR**» *(⚠ [read as* «Rogar» *on 11 October and corrected the same day](/corrections/))*, *n.* **3 Nov 1900**, *ob.* **22 Jan 1968** — *four children, 1923–1933* |
| «**Grah Antonius** p. Antonii» | *and the generation after him* — ⚠ *[living, and named only](/method/)* |

**⭐ HOUSE 38 — two more households.** *«**Grah Antonius**»,* ***sutor*** *(a shoemaker), n.* **10 Mar 1869**, *with* «**Gertrudis n. ŽUŽIĆ**», *n.* **18 Mar 1879**, *and six children 1906–1917; and* «**Grah Josephus**», *agricola, n.* **20 Sept 1867**, *with* «**Rosa n. ŠESTAN**», *n.* **23 Feb 1872*** — ⚠ **ŠESTAN is itself one of this archive's married-in surnames.**

**⭐ HOUSE 19** — «**Grah Martinus**, *viduus*, *rusticus*», *n.* **28 Oct 1827** — ***the oldest of the name in the book***. **HOUSE 23** — «**Grah Joannes def. Josephi**», *n.* **5 Sept 1852**, *with* «**Francisca n. MAREČIĆ**», *twelve children; his son* «**Josephus Grah**», *n.* **2 Feb 1900**, *with* «**Anna n. PAVLE-KRISTIĆ**». **HOUSE 53** — «**Grah Antun**», ***ferroviarius***, *whose second wife came* «***e SVETVINČENAT***» ⚠ *— [one of this archive's own parishes](/worklist/).* **AND IN THE CROATIAN HALF** — «**Grah Ana**» *(n. 1906)*, «**Grah Antun**», *radnik (n. 1908)*, *and* «**Grah Jelena**» *(n. 1879)*.

**⭐ And the family put a son into the Church.** *Among* **Grah Ana's** *children the conditio column carries the single word* «***svećenik***» — ***a priest***. ⚠ *[He is named and nothing more.](/method/)*

**⭐⭐ A daughter followed from her father's house to her husband's, inside one book.** *House* **18** *enters* «**Roža**», *n.* **13.VI.1909**, *among Matthaeus's nine children; the* **Lušetić** *household of house* **25** *enters* «***Grach Rosa fil. Matthaei***», *n.* **13.6.1909**. ***Same day, same father, two houses apart.*** *She is one of* ***eight*** *Grah daughters this book marries out — into* **Držetić**, **Dujanić**, **Šepuka**, **Opašić**, **Krošnjak** *(struck) and* **Lušetić** *twice.*

⚠ **And a Grah of house 38 married a ŠESTAN** — «**Rosa n. Šestan**», *n.* **23 Feb 1872** — ***which is one of this archive's own married-in surnames.*** ⚠ *No kinship is claimed; it is a place where two sets of records touch.*

**⭐ And five Grah daughters married out of the name at Cerovlje** — *into* **Držetić** *(Francisca)*, **Dujanić** *(Maria n.* ***Grah-Mišan***, *n. 27 Jun 1897)*, **Šepuka** *(Maria, n. 6 Feb 1882)*, **Opašić** *(Maria-Rosa, n. 15 Oct 1887, to a railway worker)* *and a struck* **Krošnjak** *entry naming a second wife née Grah, n. 6 Sept 1887.*

**⭐⭐ And the 1894 census's own REPERTORIUM gives a second Gologorica Grah.** *[M01069759, page 18, under* «G R»*](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses):* «***Grah - Missan Rosalia***», *house* **29**, *born in the* **1840s**. ***A person-level index, so it sees women under their own surnames*** — *and one Grah in two hundred and forty-six frames.* ⚠ *[The 1862 census's own* «Ordo alfabeticus familiarum» *has* **no Grah at all**](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses) — *but it indexes* ***families***, *so a Grah wife would not appear in it.*

**⚠⚠ THREE FORMS OF THE NAME, AND A SEARCH FOR ONE MISSES THE OTHERS.**

| | |
|---|---|
| «**Grah**» | *the registers' own ink, at all three parishes* |
| «**Grah-Mišan**» | *a compound with a byname attached, now attested in* ***all three parishes*** *— [Gračišće](/worklist/), [Cerovlje](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah) and [Gologorica](/gologorica-line/#sa1826grah). [The archive's one known Gologorica Grah had it all along and it went unread for eleven days.](/gologorica-line/#sa1826grah)* |
| «**Gracco**» | *the Italianised form, added in faint* ***pencil*** *above at least four Cerovlje household headings by a later hand* |

***The pencil form is the one that will cost somebody a day***: *it sits above the heading rather than in it, and it is what an Italian-era index or civil record of the 1920s and 1930s would carry.* ⚠ *And at Gračišće the Latin register writes* «**Grach**» *and* «**Grah**» *for the same couple, and once* «**Prach**» — *[tested against that scribe's own P and G and left as written](/gologorica-line/#grahgracisce).*

⚠ **A false positive worth knowing:** *in the Gračišće hand* «**CINRICH**» *reads convincingly as* «Grah» *at page scale and does not survive magnification — flagged twice and destroyed twice. [Magnify every candidate.](/method/)*

**⚠⚠ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND IS NOT CLAIMED.**

***Three populations of the name within ten kilometres — Krbune, Gračišće and Cerovlje — and no document yet joins any two of them.*** *The Krbune pair are placed there by the registers' own words; the Gračišće household is* «Cives» *and townish; the Cerovlje households are* «rustici», «sutor», «ferroviarius». **[A surname shared across parishes four kilometres apart is not a family](/method/)**, *and this archive has been caught by exactly that shape before.*

⚠ *Nor is* «***Marianna GRAH-MIŠAN ux. filia Matthiae et Justinae***», *in the Bubich household of the Gologorica* status animarum *of 1826 (M01069358), attached to any of the three.* **[The 1826 book has now been swept end to end and she is the only Grah in a hundred and twenty-one frames.](/gologorica-line/#sa1826grah)**
grach.found:
**Searched beyond the parish books, and the result is thin.** *Krbune's own register (1803–1870) is a* ***controlled nil*** *for the name — the instrument was proved against 457 Valcovich from the same film. The Gologorica death index's* «G» *block runs* **Gasparich · Gaspetich · Gherbaz · Gherfan ×2 · Giurando · Giuratich · Gregorovich** *and stops; its* Extranei *column — six people in ninety-six years — names one person from Krbune, and she is a* **Bortlich**, *not a Grah. The Gologorica obit calendar is nil on the name across every opening read.*

***Everything this archive holds for the Grah has come out of parish registers, and all of it since 9 October 2026.***
grach.next:
**Three things, in order of cheapness.**

**1 · Finish the two books that have no index.** *[Cerovlje is read end to end](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah); [the 1826 Gologorica census is read end to end](/gologorica-line/#sa1826grah). [So is the 1921 census](/gologorica-line/#sa1921grah). What is left is the* ***register frames*** *of 1862 and 1894, whose indexes were used instead — [and the 1862 index lists families, so a Grah wife is outside it](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses).*

**2 · Search under all four forms, and above the heading.** «**Grah**» · «**Grach**» · «**Grah-Mišan / Grah-Missan**» · «**Gracco**». *[The Italian form was imposed by decree and is written in pencil above the household name, where the ink search will never reach it.](/method/)*

**3 · Test the three populations against each other.** *What would join Krbune, Gračišće and Cerovlje is a* **marriage** *or a* **godparent clause** *naming a Grah of one parish in another's book. [The Gračišće marriage register is on the reel](/gologorica-line/) and has never been opened for this name. ⚠ **Until something does, they stay three families with one name.**

buich.title: Buić
buich.why: **Magdalena Buić (written Buich), born at Pomer on 11 July 1816, married Tomas Defranceschi of Pomer on 16 August 1843** and was the mother of Lucia (1844), Michele (1847) and Maria (1852). Her father, Paolo Buich, a countryman of house 28, was already dead at her marriage. The surname reaches the rest of the archive through her son **Stephanus, baptised at Pomer on 1 August 1859 to «Magdalena vidua Tomasi Defranceschi nata Buich» with no father named**, who is written Buić, and through his eight children, 1889–1908.
known: **Stephanus bears his mother's maiden surname and no father is ever named.** The 1897 baptism of his son writes him «Buich Stephanus illeg.mus». *(doc.)*

He married **Emilia née Košara**; the register spells their children Buić. One burial entry, of 1908, writes the child's surname «Defranceschi» with «Buich» added above as a correction: the only place in the Pomer books where a child of Stephanus Buić is written with the surname Defranceschi. *(doc.)*

**Magdalena's death is probably read:** the Pula civil hospital, 20 March 1898, «Defranceschi Magdalena, *vidua* Thomae, *e Pomario*, *villica*», aged 85. *(inf, strongly.)* The age is three and a half years above her baptism's, and the archive says so. The Pomer deaths books were read for the surname Defranceschi and not for Buić, so a Buić death may be in them unfound.

**Corrected 13 October 2026:** her surname was first misread from a Medulin cell, until the Pomer register gave it four times in two hands as Buić. The person's frozen id still carries the misreading; the person is unchanged.
Her daughters: **Lucia married Matheus Lazaro** at Pomer, and **Maria married Petrus Kirac** at Medulin in 1874.

lazaro.title: Lazaro
lazaro.why: **Matheus Lazaro married Lucia Defranceschi at Pomer in January 1866 (as read)**, she the daughter of Tomas Defranceschi and Magdalena Buić, and their children were baptised at Pomer from 1866 to 1884. The marriage entry writes him «Matheus Lazzaro q. Mathei», aged 29. He died on 27 September 1899, aged 62 years 11 months 20 days, and the burial entry calls him «maritus Luciae Defranceschi, agricola».
known: **He was born about 7 October 1836, not about 1843.** The «c1843» in his frozen id was a guess from the index; the marriage entry (aged 29) and the death entry (62 years 11 months) agree with each other. *(doc.)*
At the baptism of Euphemia, the first child, on 4 November 1866 he is written «Miles et Possid[ens]», a soldier and a landholder. *(doc.)*
The surname is written **Lazaro, Lazzaro and Lazar** in different entries; the father of Matheus is «Matthaei», and the mother's name was not read with confidence.
Catharina, born 1884, is written the youngest of nine children. Six of the nine have a death year in childhood on the roster (1873 to 1884); Catharina lived to 1954.

giachin.title: Giachin
giachin.why: **Two Giachin men of Vodnjan each took a De Franceschi wife.** Sebastiano Giachin and Domenica De Franceschi had four children baptised at Vodnjan, 1817–1832 (household h052). Domenico Giachin and Michiela De Franceschi had two, in 1818 and 1821 (household h060). The households list gives each couple and nothing about the husband's origin.
known: **Michiela is Michiela De Franceschi *fu Giuseppe*.** On 20 February 1833, at Vodnjan house 532, her son Giacomo died, his father already «del fu» Domenico Giachin and she still alive. The entry gives her father's name only as Giuseppe: whether she is a daughter of the Giuseppe De Franceschi (1758–1830) is an inference, and the archive marks it as one. *(doc for the entry; inf for the link.)*

There were at least three different Michiela De Franceschis at Vodnjan in these years (fu Pietro, wife of Andrea Palin; di Cristoforo; fu Giuseppe, wife of Domenico Giachin). The patronymic, not the name, is what separates them.
Domenica's birth, about 1795, is inferred from a marriage by 1816; the baptisms do not say whose daughter she was.

The Vodnjan *Liber Copulatorum* opens in October 1815; the Giachin marriage is not among the fourteen De Franceschi marriages catalogued from it (1817–1832), so it lies in the book's first fifteen months or before the book begins.

chersin.title: Chersin
chersin.from: Pula and Fažana, where Natale Defranceschi's household is recorded, 1849–1851
chersin.why: **Domenica Chersin was the wife of Natale Defranceschi**, in a household recorded at Pula (h034) and again at Fažana (h035), mother of Vittorio Giovanni (born 1849) and Angelo (born 1851). The archive's marriage index counts **eight indexed marriages** with the surname Chersin and groups it as Venetian by its form, which the archive itself calls «a reading, not a finding»; the one Chersin it has placed lived in Austrian Istria.
known: **Her birth is unknown.** The year 1851 was carried as her birth year and was corrected on 13 September 2026: it is the year she first appears, in the baptism of her eldest known child.

Two of the three entries are the household list (Pula h034, Fažana h035), index only; the third is from David's tree and sits at Draguč. The archive's own note on the tree entry ties her to the household of 1849–1851.

An **open question** hangs on her family: whether the Angelo Defranceschi, 63, of via del Prato, Pola, who was taken to the hospital in November 1914, is her son Angelo, born 1851. It is an inference and is labelled one.
Forebears counts 109 living bearers of the surname in the world: Italy 65, United States 20, Romania 14, Croatia 7.

caneva.title: De Caneva
caneva.from: Liariis, in the commune of Ovaro, Carnia
caneva.why: **Lucia Santa, daughter of the late Osvaldo Antonio de Caneva of Liariis, married Felice Santo de Franceschi, a weaver (*tessitore*), at Ovaro on 15 June 1815.** Her mother, Lucia Colinassio, widow of Osvaldo Antonio, was present in person on 14 June to consent. The act writes the family «de Canova» and the baptismal extract writes it «De Caneva». The bride could not sign: «dichiara essere illetterata».
known: The act declares all four witnesses «non parenti, né affini». One of them is **Daniele «del fu Osvaldo» de Canova**, 49, *possidente* of Liariis, born about 1766, twenty-seven years before the bride.
**An open question:** either there were two men called Osvaldo at Liariis, or the «non parenti» formula is boilerplate and Daniele is the bride's brother.
The de Caneva of Liariis are well recorded: a Gio: Batta De Caneva stood godfather in 1793, and Jacoba, widow of Nicolaus de Caneva, in 1769.
The family listed below is the bride's, not the groom's.

corva.title: Corva
corva.from: Muina, in the commune of Ovaro, Carnia
corva.why: **Maria, daughter of the late Giacomo Corva of Muina, married Antonio de Franceschi of Gologorica at Svetvinčenat on 14 March 1785.** She was living in the Svetvinčenat parish when she married, though of Muina by origin, and her banns were read at Muina. The archive identifies her, as an inference, with the Maria née Corva who is the mother of Osvaldo de Franceschi of Muina, and who by January 1808 was «vedova del fu Antonio de Franceschi». *(doc for the entry; inf for the identification.)*
known: **Her father Giacomo Corva is named in this archive for the first time in that entry, and was already dead in 1785.** The Carnia page had her only as «Maria née Corva», with no marriage found and no father's name.

The marriages essay names Corva and Crosilla together as the Carnian surnames that are Carnian in more than shape: in the scholarship on the Canale di Gorto emigration they are families of Ovaro's own commune, and a Giovanni Corva of Muina held tenants at Agrons.

A stone in the Carnian cemeteries reads **CORVA MARIANNA 1896–1979**, beside De Franceschi Umberto 1892–1988. The photographs do not distinguish which of the four cemeteries (Ovaro, Mione, Muina, Agrons) it stands in, and the archive does not guess. *(doc for the inscription.)*
The Muina marriage papers of 1806–07 hold two marriages of other Muina families, one of them a Corva, and no De Franceschi.

crosilla.title: Crosilla
crosilla.from: Mione and Liariis, in the commune of Ovaro, Carnia
crosilla.why: **Crosilla is one of the two in-married surnames the archive's marriages essay calls Carnian in more than shape.** The essay says the scholarship on the Canale di Gorto emigration names it as a family of Ovaro's own commune, and that the *Micoli Crosilla Toscano* were the leading house of **Mione**, who built the *casa delle cento finestre* and ran a cloth shop at Pinguente. In Istria, two Crosilla husbands are recorded with a Defranceschi wife, and the essay adds that a Jacobina Defranceschi, born 1804, was buried in 1882 as the wife of a Joan-Baptae Crosilla.
known: Two households, both **index only: no register read**: Gio Battista Crosilla and Giacoma De Franceschi (h025, two children, 1825 and 1831, at «Croazia, Austria» as the index puts it) and Joan Baptista Crosilla and Jacoba Defranceschi (h063; the index names him as father on two baptisms, 1833–1845).

In Carnia, the name stands twice among the witnesses at the Ovaro wedding of 1815 (Crisilla: Giovanni del fu Giacomo, 69, *possidente*, and Giacomo del fu Nicolò, 69, *falegname*), and **Orsola née Crosilla**, of Liariis stock, is the wife of Pietro Ermanni of Mione. *(doc.)*
**Giovanni Micoli-Toscano** was godfather to Felice Santo de Franceschi on 2 November 1792, of the family whose Mione palace holds the 1679 weavers' contracts. *(doc.)*
A stone reads **ANNA CROSILLA ved. SORAVITO DE FRANCESCHI 1900–1990**; the photographs do not say in which of the four Carnian cemeteries it stands. *(doc for the inscription.)*
The essay's own verdict on the Istrian burial: «not proof of descent», and it adds, «a very loud coincidence».

close:
**Three of the six women who married into our own direct line are not in this index at all.** *Peschle*, *Fernasar* and *Kovačina* appear below with a count of zero — not because those marriages did not happen, but because the indexed marriage set does not contain them. Two of the three are mothers of generations of this line. It is a useful reminder of what a count on this page is actually measuring: **not marriages, but marriages somebody has indexed.**

**Fourteen of the seventy-one carry Carnian surnames** — Cerlon, Francin, Tamborin, Bonassin, Dorliguzzo, Cleva, Elegnan, Ceselin and more. If this family came out of Carnia and went on marrying other Carnian families in Istria, that is exactly the pattern it would leave. It is also exactly what surname-morphology guessing produces when you go looking for it, and this archive has never tested a single one of them against a Carnian register. **It is the best lead on the page and the least worked.**

fbnote.heading: And what a surname atlas can and cannot settle
fbnote.text:
Every family above was put in its group by **how the surname looks** — the archive's own caveat calls that *«a reading, not a finding»*. On 14 September 2026 the reading was tested against **forebears.io**, which counts living bearers of a surname by country. Where a figure exists it is shown on the row.

**It settles less than it looks as though it should, and the reason matters.** A Carnian family that came down into Istria in 1700 and stayed has descendants who are Croatian today. So *Bonassin* standing at **Croatia 76, Italy 49**, and *Vellico* at **Croatia 40, Italy 34**, are not evidence against a Friulian origin — **they are what a Friulian origin plus this exact migration would produce.** The atlas measures where people are now; this archive is asking where they came from, and for these families those are different questions by design.

**Where it does bite is the rare names, and there it is decisive.** *Dorliguzzo* has **ten bearers in the world**. *Ceselin* has fifty-eight, all Italian. *Cerlon* has eighty-five. Those are village surnames, and a village surname that survives in Italy and Croatia and nowhere else is doing exactly what the Carnia-to-Istria account says it should.

**And it flags two groupings that look wrong.** *Francin* is **France 332, Italy 10** — filed here as Carnian on the strength of its ending. *Primus* is **United States 3,154, Tanzania 1,106, Germany 652**, with no Adriatic centre at all, and is filed as Venetian. In both cases the likeliest explanation is that a rare local name collides with a common name elsewhere and the global figures drown it — but the classification rests on nothing else, and it is now marked.

**Three names have no bearers anywhere**: *Fernasar*, *Bellinich* and *Elegnan*. For **Bellinich** and **Elegnan** that stands. For **Fernasar** it does not, and the correction is worth making here: it returns nothing on Hungaricana, but the **Austrian press has it three times** — *Il Giornaletto di Pola* in 1914 and two Vienna casualty lists — so it is a real Istrian surname that has simply died out. See its own page. **Peschle**, the mother of Carlo De Franceschi's own family, is down to **one bearer in the world**.
